newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog calls comments on digital TV access.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog calls comments on digital TV access.

text.p: UK telecommunications regulator Oftel on Thursday published a consultative document which it said should give the industry confidence ahead of the launch of digital broadcasting within the next year or so.

Oftel plans to ensure than the control of conditional access technology, or digital receiver set-top boxes, is not used to distort, restrict or prevent competition in television and other content services.
BSkyB, the dominant force in British pay television, is planning to launch a digital satellite service with up to 200 channels in late 1997.
Digital terrestrial television -- broadcast from land-based transmitters -- is set to begin in mid-1998, offering a further 35 or so channels.
Some broadcasters had expressed fears that BSkyB would be able to exploit its "first-mover" status to gain a stranglehold on the digital environment.
To unscramble signals and receive any of the new services, audiences will need a digital receiver -- available first as a "set-top" box and later inside digital televisions.
Oftel director general Don Cruickshank called for comments on what sort of subsidy consumer set-top boxes would need.
Cruickshank is also looking into various ways of recovering that subsidy through charges to broadcasters.

Other issues he wants discussed include how broadcasters can gain access to electronic programme guides so that viewers are not "unduly influenced" in their programme choice by the order and prominence of information within a guide.

Another issue raised by access technology to digital television is how broadcasters can use the services and still keep their subscriber base confidential while operators of conditional access systems can keep control of their intellectual property.

Oftel also wants to discuss whether there are likely to be any capacity constraints in conditional access systems and how the price of these services can ensure that they are offered on "fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory" terms.
Oftel, which is calling for comments by January 24, 1997, is keen that consumers should have uncomplicated access to a wide range of digital services without "unnecessary" additional expense.
The watchdog also wants to ensure that control of conditional access technology does not lead to any artificial restrictions on consumers' choice of equipment. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 4365
